topic: Llama 4 Scout vs Maverick: Complete API Developer Guide

key_points: Meta announced Scout, Maverick, and Behemoth as the first Llama 4 releases, with Scout and Maverick available immediately on Meta channels.
Behemoth was stated as in training and delayed, framing the practical API landscape around Scout + Maverick only.
TechCrunch frames the release as open-source/partner-first and highlights model size positioning (Scout 17B active/109B total, Maverick 17B active/400B total).
Introduces Scout as large-file oriented while Maverick is conversation-oriented, giving a clean split for API use-case selection.
Places Llama 4 as Meta’s new MoE baseline and reinforces that Behemoth is previewed but not immediately available.
Useful for positioning a practical “which model to serve” decision tree.
Frames Llama 4 as part of competitive pressure against DeepSeek-era open models and emphasizes flagship positioning.
Reinforces public parameter narrative used by downstream guides for comparison headlines and benchmark framing.
Useful for article positioning section around model-era context and why Scout/Maverick matter to API builders.
Confirms managed availability in Amazon Bedrock and Amazon SageMaker, including multimodal support and enterprise deployment positioning.
Highlights practical context window note: AWS describes 3.5M context for Scout in Bedrock while Meta advertises 10M (important implementation caveat).
Provides a real deployment-oriented baseline: serverless Bedrock access plus enterprise scaling tradeoffs.
NVIDIA positions both models as native multimodal MoE with major throughput improvements on Blackwell/H100/FP8 stacks.
Includes concrete throughput and serving guidance, making it useful for latency-sensitive API architecture sections.
Shows how infrastructure-first guidance can outperform purely benchmark-first comparisons.

stats.fact: Meta announced Llama 4 on Apr 5, 2025; Scout and Maverick are the first release models, with Behemoth not yet generally released.
Official specs: Llama 4 Scout has 17B active parameters, 16 experts, and a 10M token context window.
Official specs: Llama 4 Maverick has 17B active parameters, 128 experts, and a 1M token context window in AWS model card details.
NVIDIA reports Scout optimized to single H100 with int4 and benchmarked over 40K output tokens/sec on Blackwell B200, while Maverick reached over 30K on the same stack.
Meta notes MoE architecture enables fixed-FLOP efficiency gains; Llama 4 used iRoPE and long-context training changes, plus more than 30T tokens in the training mixture.
Meta’s AWS announcement claims near 80x context increase vs Llama 3 for Scout (128K → 10M), and quantifies multimodal, single H100-friendly deployment.
AWS model cards list a max output limit of 8K tokens and model launch date Apr 05, 2025; standard tiers include Converse/Chat style access options through bedrock-runtime.

angles: Model selection is no longer only about raw benchmark rank: Scout’s 10M context and maverick’s image-focused multimodal strength create distinct routing profiles for API architectures.
Provider implementations differ (e.g., AWS Bedrock context caps vs official model docs), so production teams should benchmark per provider endpoint, not per paper spec.
API ecosystems now span managed (Bedrock, watsonx) and inference-optimized (NVIDIA NIM/OpenAI-compat) paths, enabling mixed deployment strategies for resilience.
MoE architecture plus native multimodality is now mainstream in open-weights, which shifts design toward structured multimodal pipelines (text+image + retrieval) over plain text prompts.
Cost/performance narratives are converging: benchmark leadership is less useful without endpoint-level throughput and token limits for each provider.
